title: The comparison bound on coefficients of étale origin is $M=0$
statement:
Let $X$ be any scheme and $A$ a finite discrete commutative ring. Use sheaves of modules over the constant sheaves $A_{X_{\mathrm{et}}}$ and $A_{X_{\mathrm{proet}}}$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], on the small sites [def-weil-pbc-etale-site, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Let $
u_X:X_{\mathrm{proet}}	o X_{\mathrm{et}}$ be the comparison geometric morphism [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]. Its inverse image on fixed-$A$ modules, denoted $
u_X^*$, applies the inverse image to the underlying abelian sheaf and to each scalar endomorphism; its direct image $
u_{X,*}$ is restriction to etale objects. Right derived functors are computed by injective module resolutions [def-sp-left-exact-additive, def-sp-injective-resolutions]. For every sheaf $G$ of $A$-modules on $X_{\mathrm{et}}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves], the adjunction unit and higher direct images satisfy
$$G\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }
u_{X,*}
u_X^*G,\qquad R^q
u_{X,*}(
u_X^*G)=0\quad(q>0).$$
No constructibility or finiteness hypothesis is imposed on $G$, and no Noetherian or dimension hypothesis is imposed on $X$. In particular the comparison direct image has bound $M=0$ on sheaves of etale origin: any $F$ isomorphic to $
u_X^*G$ has $R^q
u_{X,*}F=0$ for $q>0$, independently of $\dim X$. For a finite field $\mathbf F_q$ of characteristic $p$, $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, a prime $\ell
e p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, $n\geq1$, $A=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n\mathcal O_E$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], and a finite-type $k$-scheme $X$, this applies to every coefficient sheaf of [def-sf-fullcd-used-class] by its defining etale-origin witness.

proof.text: Write $L=\nu_X^{-1}$ and $R=\nu_{X,*}$ on abelian sheaves, and $L_A,R_A$ for the fixed-$A$ module functors. For the constant sheaf $\underline A$ of [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], giving an $\underline A$-module structure on an abelian sheaf is equivalent to giving compatible endomorphisms $\lambda_a$ for all $a\in A$ satisfying the module identities. Indeed, [lem-pc-sites-sheafification-underlying-sets] identifies the underlying set sheafification of the constant ring presheaf, and [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheafification-sections-local] applied to the constant presheaf says that a section of $\underline A$ is locally represented by constants, with equal representatives agreeing after a further cover. Act by those constants on that cover and glue. Two presentations agree after a common refinement, so the result is well-defined. A map commuting with all $\lambda_a$ is therefore linear over every section of $\underline A$, by restriction to such a cover and the sheaf uniqueness axiom. This applies on both sites for the finite discrete ring $A$. By [lem-cbc-comparison-pullback-sections], at every etale object $U$ the comparison unit on underlying sets identifies $G(U)$ with $(L_AG)(U)$. The algebraic-structure construction of [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism] applies the set inverse image to addition, zero, negation and every endomorphism $\lambda_a$ for $a\in A$. The finite set of scalar operations is carried along by the finite-limit-preserving inverse image, and applying it to each module identity gives the same identity after pullback. The unit is natural in these operations, so its component at $U$ is $A$-linear. Its bijective inverse is $A$-linear, since for $y=\eta_U(x)$ one has $\eta_U^{-1}(ay)=\eta_U^{-1}(\eta_U(ax))=ax$. These inverses commute with restrictions by the naturality of $\eta$. The module convention [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and the preceding local scalar argument therefore give the asserted unit isomorphism over the constant ring sheaf. The set-sheaf adjunction restricts to the module adjunction: a map and its transpose commute with addition and each $\lambda_a$ by naturality of the unit and counit, and the module identities are preserved by the finite-product-preserving inverse image. Thus the map just checked is its actual unit for this finite discrete $A$. For an abelian etale sheaf $B$, the same cited sections formula makes $\eta_B:B\to RLB$ an objectwise bijection. Naturality with respect to addition, zero and negation makes each component a group homomorphism; its inverse is a group homomorphism and commutes with restrictions. Hence $\eta_B$ is an isomorphism of abelian sheaves. Naturality in a morphism $b:B\to B'$ says $(RLb)\eta_B=\eta_{B'}b$.

proof.text: For an arbitrary abelian sheaf $B$ on $X_{\mathrm{et}}$, choose an injective resolution $B\to I^\bullet$, using enough injectives on sites in [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. By [lem-weil-pbc-site-pullback-abelian-exact], $LB\to LI^\bullet$ is an exact resolution. Each $LI^n$ is $R$-acyclic by [lem-cbc-abelian-comparison-injective-acyclicity]. Clause (2) of [lemma-weil-pbc-leray-acyclicity] computes $R^qR(LB)$ by $\mathcal H^q(RLI^\bullet)$. The natural unit isomorphisms from step 1 commute with the differentials of $I^\bullet$, so $RLI^\bullet\cong I^\bullet$ as complexes. Since $I^\bullet$ resolves $B$ in degree zero, $R^qR(LB)=0$ for every $q>0$. This is the independent acyclicity argument needed in addition to ordinary full faithfulness.

source.place: Tag 099V, label lemma-relative-comparison, second paragraph; acyclic resolutions: derived.tex, Tag 015E, label lemma-leray-acyclicity

proof.text: Work in one sufficiently large universe for both small-site representatives and all coefficient values. By [lem-pur-ringed-site-grothendieck-abelian] and [lem-sp-grothendieck-enough-injectives], the categories of module sheaves over the constant ring $A$ on these sites have enough injectives. Direct image $R_A$ is additive and left exact: it restricts module sheaves to etale objects, so it preserves zero, addition and the sectionwise kernels specified in [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Let $S_{\mathrm{proet}}$ and $S_{\mathrm{et}}$ forget scalars. They are exact and faithful by [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful]. If $J$ is an injective pro-etale $A$-module sheaf, then for every pro-etale object $W$ and $q>0$, [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-site-module-abelian-evaluation-comparison] identifies $H^q(W,S_{\mathrm{proet}}J)$ with $R^q\Gamma_{\mathrm{Mod}}(W,J)=0$: the latter is computed using the injective resolution having just $J$ in degree zero. In particular this holds at every etale object $u_X(U)$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-site-higher-direct-image-sheafified-presheaf] to the abelian comparison functor $R$: its positive higher direct image of $S_{\mathrm{proet}}J$ is the sheafification of the zero presheaf $U\mapsto H^q(u_X(U),S_{\mathrm{proet}}J)$. Thus $S_{\mathrm{proet}}J$ is $R$-acyclic. This proves the needed acyclicity without asserting that $S_{\mathrm{proet}}J$ is injective.

proof.text: For a pro-etale module sheaf $M$, choose an injective module resolution $M\to J^\bullet$. Exactness of $S_{\mathrm{proet}}$ from [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful] makes $S_{\mathrm{proet}}M\to S_{\mathrm{proet}}J^\bullet$ an abelian resolution; step 3 makes every term $R$-acyclic. Thus [lemma-weil-pbc-leray-acyclicity] (2) computes $R^qR(S_{\mathrm{proet}}M)$ as $\mathcal H^q(RS_{\mathrm{proet}}J^\bullet)$. Restriction to etale objects gives equality $RS_{\mathrm{proet}}J^\bullet=S_{\mathrm{et}}R_AJ^\bullet$ by the direct-image formula of [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]. Exactness of $S_{\mathrm{et}}$ preserves the kernels and images defining cohomology, so the last cohomology sheaf is $S_{\mathrm{et}}\mathcal H^q(R_AJ^\bullet)=S_{\mathrm{et}}R^qR_A(M)$, by [def-sp-left-exact-additive]. Now put $M=L_AG$. The scalar construction in step 1 identifies $S_{\mathrm{proet}}L_AG=L(S_{\mathrm{et}}G)$. Step 2 says the abelian higher direct images of this sheaf are zero. Hence $S_{\mathrm{et}}R^qR_A(L_AG)=0$ for $q>0$. A module sheaf with zero underlying abelian sheaf has zero sections on every object and is itself zero. This proves the desired module vanishing for every finite discrete commutative $A$.

source.place: Tag 03FD, label lemma-cohomology-modules-abelian-agree, acyclic-resolution argument combined with proetale.tex Tag 099V

proof.text: If $F\cong L_AG$, functoriality of each $R^qR_A$ carries this isomorphism to $R^qR_AF\cong R^qR_A(L_AG)=0$ for $q>0$. Thus $M=0$ works for the whole etale-origin class, with no dependence on dimension. For the coefficient class [def-sf-fullcd-used-class], take a finite field $\mathbf F_q$ of characteristic $p$, $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, $n\geq1$, $A=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$, and a finite-type $k$-scheme $\overline X$. By [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], $A$ is a finite commutative ring, taken with its discrete topology, so steps 1--4 apply. The defining condition of the class is $\mathcal F\cong\nu_{\overline X}^*\mathcal G$; this is precisely such an origin witness. This defining condition is the whole membership condition in the current statement of that node. The argument proves a bound for the comparison functor; a dimension bound for a proper morphism is a separate statement.

blueprint_update.statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme and let $\nu_X:X_{\Proet}\to X_{\Et}$ be the comparison
morphism of [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism], the coefficient ring
being $A$. Let $G$ be a sheaf of $A$-modules on the small étale site
$X_{\Et}$, in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves]; *no*
constructibility hypothesis is imposed on $G$. Then the adjunction map

$$
G\longrightarrow\nu_{X,*}\nu_X^*G
$$

is an isomorphism, and consequently

$$
R^q\nu_{X,*}\bigl(\nu_X^*G\bigr)=0\qquad(q>0).
$$

Thus on the sheaves of étale origin – equivalently, by
[lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin], on the coefficient sheaves of the
blueprint's class [def-sf-fullcd-used-class] – the vanishing degree of
the comparison direct image is bounded by $M=0$, independently of the
dimension of $X$ and of any constructibility of $G$.

proof.text:
The two inputs are Bhatt–Scholze, Lemma 5.1.1 and Corollary 5.1.6 of
[arXiv:1309.1198v2](https://arxiv.org/html/1309.1198v2), quoted verbatim in
Section 16.1 of the audit ledger; both are stated for an arbitrary scheme and
an arbitrary sheaf, respectively bounded-below complex, on the small étale
site, so a sheaf of $A$-modules on $X_{\Et}$ in the sense of
[def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves] is covered verbatim. By Lemma 5.1.1, for
$G\in\Sh(X_{\Et})$ and an affine pro-étale $U=\lim_iU_i$ one has
$\nu_X^*G(U)=\colim_iG(U_i)$, the presheaf so defined being a sheaf; by
Lemma 5.1.2 the pullback $\nu_X^*$ is fully faithful, with essential image
exactly those sheaves $F$ on $X_{\Proet}$ whose values on $U=\lim_iU_i$
are the filtered colimits of their values on the $U_i$. The sheaf
$\nu_X^*G$ lies in that essential image, so
$\nu_X^*\nu_{X,*}\nu_X^*G\to\nu_X^*G$ is an isomorphism; applying the fully
faithful $\nu_X^*$ to the two maps $G\to\nu_{X,*}\nu_X^*G$ and
$\nu_{X,*}\nu_X^*G\to G$ that this isomorphism exhibits shows that the
adjunction map $G\to\nu_{X,*}\nu_X^*G$ is an isomorphism in
$\Sh(X_{\Et},A)$. Corollary 5.1.6 is the derived form of the same identity:
$K\to R\nu_{X,*}\nu_X^*K$ is an equivalence for every
$K\in D^+(X_{\Et})$. Taking $K=G$ concentrated in degree zero and passing
to cohomology sheaves gives
$R^q\nu_{X,*}\nu_X^*G=\mathcal H^q(R\nu_{X,*}\nu_X^*G)=0$ for every $q>0$,
which is the displayed vanishing. The identification of the class of étale
origin with the coefficient class [def-sf-fullcd-used-class] is
[lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin], and the passage from this bound to
the bound $2d$ of [thm-sf-fullcd-etale-origin] in the form of
[def-weil-full-cohomological-dimension] is through the Leray spectral
sequence of [thm-sp-grothendieck], whose $p$-direction is bounded by
$2d$ on the étale site.
